description: Trigger and behavior cases for property-based test design: domain invariants per target, bounded generator domains with shrinking, counterexample triage, runner handoff, and routing away from per-change plans, test-data design, test-file writing and flake repair.

cases.prompt: Design property-based coverage for our CSV parser — which invariants should hold for every input, and what should the generators look like?

assertions: States domain invariants (for example parse-then-print round-trips and quoted-field handling) that do not restate the implementation.
Names the generator domains with bounds and the shrink direction per property.
Defines counterexample triage and names the runner handoff without writing or running anything.

cases.prompt: Design property-based tests for our order state machine — what invariants hold across every transition sequence?

assertions: States transition-sequence invariants (for example: no transition reaches a forbidden state; cancelled orders cannot be paid) with bounded transition-sequence generators and shrinking.
Keeps the properties domain-derived rather than copied from the implementation.

cases.prompt: Write the vitest property test file for the CSV parser and run it.

assertions: Does not invoke this skill; writing and running the test files belongs to vitest-unit-component-engineer.

cases.prompt: Add property-based testing to our codebase.

assertions: Halts and asks which unit or module the properties should cover.
Does not invent targets from the codebase name.

cases.prompt: Design the property tests for the invoice amount math, then write the test file and run the suite.

assertions: Produces the design, then stops at implementation: writing and running the suite is vitest-unit-component-engineer (manual-only) and is handed off by name, not executed in the same pass.
States the handoff explicitly rather than silently dropping the implementation half of the ask.
